statement: --t1: T1 full head input (not bias corrected), requiring an absolute path.
Optional T2 full-head input must be externally biasfield corrected when --no_biasfield is used.
An optional binary lesion mask must be in the same space as the T1 input.
For --surf_only, the segmentation created by FastSurferVINN must already exist.
A segmentation without --tal_reg does not need a FreeSurfer licence.
Docker runs of the surface module require --fs_license pointing to a FreeSurfer licence file.
Input conformation specifications are checked automatically; non-compliant images are conformed.
Keeping native image geometry is incompatible with the surface pipeline.
A GPU makes segmentation much faster.
--viewagg_device auto checks whether there is enough memory to run view aggregation on the GPU.
Unless --ignore_fs_version is set, the program checks the FreeSurfer version and terminates if the supported version is not sourced.
--qc_snap creates quality control images to simplify the QC process.
For images with tumors or other large lesions, review LIT-modified outputs before downstream use.
Without --no_cereb, CerebNet runs automatically whenever the segmentation module runs.
Without --no_hypothal, HypVINN runs automatically whenever the segmentation module runs.
With --no_biasfield, HypVINN still runs but expects biasfields to be corrected externally.
--no_surfreg skips surface registration, but sphere.reg is needed for cross-subject statistical analysis of thickness maps.
Renaming an output file can break a later step, since later modules and follow-up tools look for the default names.
The input data file has each frame as a separate input.
Global design matrix specified with a FreeSurfer Group Descriptor File (FSGDF).
One or more contrast matrix files in ASCII text.
Surface-based smoothing requires --surf; otherwise the input is treated as a volume.
Data must be assembled by resampling each subject's data into a common space and concatenating subjects into a single file.
The same FSGD used with mris_preproc must be used, maintaining subject order.
DODS is specified in the tutorial example and is the default.
If data have not been cached, the same operations can be performed manually.
The completed GLM has its output subdirectory under the glm directory.
There is a subdirectory for each specified contrast, named after the contrast matrix file without the .mtx extension.
mri_info can be run on the assembled data to find its dimensions.
Temporary directories or log files starting with tmp may appear and can be ignored.
You cannot specify both --X and --osgm, and a contrast cannot be specified with --osgm.
Do not use --prune with --sim; instead run the non-sim analysis with --prune and pass the created mask to the simulation.
A surface file to measure for -surface-vertex-areas.
An input metric file for -metric-stats.
Optional ROI metric file restricting which data are considered.
Exactly one of -reduce or -percentile must be specified for -metric-stats.
The percentile must be between 0 and 100.
The reduction operation must be selected from the documented allowed list.
The NMT v2 template and its accompanying matching CHARM dataset, obtained from the NMT download.
The NMT download also includes a CSV table file of the ROI labels, hierarchically organized.
The CHARM is defined in the coordinates/space of the NMT v2 template.
For each form/variant of the NMT (symmetry/asymmetry, FOV, voxel size), there is a matching CHARM dataset.
The -sym option is valid for the NMT v2 only; in other cases it is ignored.
The -overwrite option allows the script to remove a pre-existing NMT directory.
AFNI uses zero-base counting, so CHARM Level 1 is volume "[0]" and Level 6 is volume "[5]".
